title: KV-aware kernel slot orchestrator for continuous batching
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Improves continuous batching fairness and reduces starvation for KV-heavy mixed workloads by routing requests to kernel variants and introducing a slot orchestration layer. No user-facing API changes; configurable opt-in via runtime config flag.
description:
Motivation: In the continuous batcher we saw intermittent tail latency spikes and starvation for low-priority streams when KV-heavy requests acquired kernel slots for prolonged periods and prevented memory-light kernels from making progress. This change introduces a lightweight orchestration layer that tags requests by KV intensity, selects kernel variants proactively, and enforces soft kernel-slot reservations to preserve fairness without hard preemption.

What I changed: Implemented a KV-aware kernel slot orchestrator that sits between the admission controller and the kernel selector. The orchestrator: 1) classifies incoming requests into intensity buckets (KV-light, KV-moderate, KV-heavy) using an inexpensive heuristic based on expected KV cache hits and input size; 2) maps buckets to preferred kernel variants (fast-path, memory-conservative, fallback); 3) maintains a small set of time-windowed kernel slots per worker to ensure progress for low-intensity lanes; 4) applies bounded preemption: long-running KV-heavy slots are given a grace window and after that are nudged to a low-priority queue with a warmup token so they can be salvaged without starving other lanes.

Additional safeguards: - Introduced jittered grace timeouts to avoid synchronized eviction waves. - Added a KV-prefetch hint path so requests likely to hit KV cache can be prepared on a background I/O lane, reducing kernel hold time. - Exposed a runtime flag to enable/disable per-worker slot orchestration for gradual rollout.

Benchmarks: Microbenchmarks on a 4xA100 cluster using a mixed workload (60% generation short prompt, 40% KV-augmented long context) show: - 95th percentile token latency reduced by ~18% (from 420ms to 345ms) for low-intensity requests when orchestration is enabled. - Overall throughput (tokens/s) unchanged within noise (+1.7%). - GPU kernel occupancy improved marginally (avg SM utilization +3%) because heavy kernels are better packed.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests cover orchestrator classification, slot accounting, and preemption paths. Added integration canary that runs in perf-canary cluster for 48h under mixed load (ENG-9876). CI gates include lint, unit, integration, and perf smoke tests. Rollout plan: enable opt-in flag in staging, run 72h canary, then enable for 20% of mainline fleet before full rollout.

Notes for reviewers: - The kernel selector changes are mostly API shims to accept an intensity tag; the fallback behavior is identical if orchestration is disabled. - KV cache manager change is additive (prefetch hint) and does not alter eviction. - This PR intentionally keeps preemption soft (no signal-based kill) due to complexity across different model runtimes.

Related: ENG-9876 (continuous-batcher starvation investigations), ENG-10021 (kernel-variant selection).

review_comments: Marco Herrera: Can you clarify how intensity buckets are computed? The heuristic should be cheap and robust under jitter.

Aisha Patel: The heuristic is a weighted score of (prompt length, expected KV keys touched, presence of long context). Implemented as a tunable linear model in cache_manager.rs with a fast-path cutoff; added comment and unit tests.
Lena Chu: We should be careful about metric cardinality; do we emit a label per bucket?
Aisha Patel: We emit a small fixed enum label (kv_intensity) with three values to keep cardinality low; added metrics docs and counters in orchestrator_metrics.go.
Omar Farouk: Is the grace timeout per-worker configurable? Could be useful for enterprise Dedicated where latency SLOs vary.
Aisha Patel: Yes — exposed the window and jitter parameters via runtime config/flags with sensible defaults; documented in docs/runtime/kv-orchestrator.md.
Marco Herrera: Approve after addressing the race condition you fixed in the last commit. Please run the 48h canary and paste perf links in the PR notes.
Aisha Patel: 48h canary completed; attached perf summary URL in the final comment and added to release notes.
CI Bot: All checks passed on merge.
notes: This PR targets a common pain point in mixed KV+generation workloads. Opt-in rollout and backward compatibility maintained. Follow-up work: explore stronger preemption primitives and per-model kernel hints (ENG-10100).
changelog_entry: runtime: add KV-aware kernel slot orchestrator to reduce starvation in continuous batching (opt-in, default off initially)
risk_assessment: Low-to-moderate: changes are behind a feature flag and non-breaking. Main risk is subtle race in slot accounting; mitigated by locks and added unit tests. Canary required before full rollout.
